solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Intricate feline parts fell in

indicators.note: the feline splits the other piece open, sitting in its middle and parting its letters

parts.note: to fall in with a plan is to go along with it, so fell in means complied
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: Bits of a cat have tumbled inside somewhere, a messy and tangled business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell in' looks like falling, but it is the military sense of falling in line: obeyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intricate has many interlocking parts and is hard to follow, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Cry of bird — motherless one?

indicators.note: lacking its mother, so the letters MA, a familiar word for mother, are dropped

parts.note: one refers back to the bird of the clue: a macaw, the big parrot

explanation.surface: A bird's call, and a question whether this is a bird with no mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for a bird again: the macaw, which loses MA, a common word for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The harsh call of a crow or rook is written as this word, a bird's cry.

clue.text: Sentimental character from Olympus retiring

parts.note: Olympus is in Greece, so its character is a Greek letter: mu
a retiring person is shy

explanation.surface: A god from Mount Olympus who goes off quietly into retirement, perhaps teary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' tempts as a reversal or a leaving signal; here it simply means bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: Mushy means soppy or over-sentimental, as in a mushy love song.

clue.text: Less sensible place to go: area in Wigan booked

parts.note: a loo is the toilet, the place you go when you need to go
Wigan Pier is the place named in the title of Orwell's book The Road to Wigan Pier, so it is a part of Wigan put in a book

explanation.surface: Somewhere to relieve yourself in Wigan has been reserved, a daft choice of venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Wigan is a town in north-west England; 'booked' points to George Orwell's 1937 book The Road to Wigan Pier, not a reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: Loopy is slang for crazy, so the comparative form means crazier, less sensible.

clue.text: Hot refreshment in mug during church function

indicators.note: the mug comes during the church, held between its two letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a mug is a fool, an ass
a role is a function or job

explanation.surface: Tea in a mug at a church social, the hot drink handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot refreshment in mug' reads as a cuppa; the mug is a fool and the refreshment is food.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew baked in a lidded dish is served piping hot as a meal.

clue.text: Shade, metallic grey, oddly

parts.note: tin is a metal, so a tin roof is a metallic one

indicators.note: taking the first and third letters, the odd-numbered positions, of the word grey

explanation.surface: A colour described as a metallic grey, with something odd about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metallic grey' reads as one colour; the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace of colour, a shade or tint.

clue.text: Anguish of the Gascon duo

parts.note: Gascony is in France, so a Gascon speaks French, where 'of the' is des
a duo is a pair

explanation.surface: The torment suffered by a pair of men from Gascony.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is utter hopelessness, a deep anguish of mind.

clue.text: Back to be dealt with by churl

indicators.note: back means the letters come in reverse, read from the end to the start

parts.note: FAO, for the attention of, marks a letter or memo as to be dealt with by someone

explanation.surface: A rude peasant is told he must deal with something when he gets back.
explanation.walkthrough: FAO is the label 'for the attention of' on mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A churl is a boorish, ill-mannered person, a lout or clumsy oaf.

clue.text: Exercise too much in public, then shower?

parts.note: overt means done openly, in public
a shower is a short spell of rain

explanation.surface: Someone works out to excess in public and then needs a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: The shower is the weather, not the gym one.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes who train too hard and too often harm their bodies by overdoing it.

clue.text: Prediction of upcoming changes in theatre assignments?

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word of is read from bottom to top

parts.note: recasting is giving the parts in a play to different actors

explanation.surface: A forecast of who will be playing which part next season at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' looks like part of the definition, the future; it turns 'of' round.
explanation.definitionFit: Forecasting is foretelling the future, as weather forecasting does.

clue.text: Triumph, confining prisoners on island state

indicators.note: the triumph confines the rest, holding them inside its letters

parts.note: to triumph is to win

indicators.note: in an across clue the prisoners come on, after, the island

parts.note: cons are convicts, prisoners

explanation.surface: A victory over an island prison where convicts are confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Fine rank

definitions.meaning: fine in the sense of thin and delicate, like a see-through fabric
rank in the sense of utter or downright, as in rank stupidity

explanation.surface: Two words: a fine, sheer quality and a rank, sheer one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer stockings are fine, and sheer folly is rank or absolute folly.

clue.text: Delay, hoping to gain from peak hours when son's away

indicators.note: the son is away, so his letter is gone from the phrase

parts.note: peak hours are a busy time

explanation.surface: A worker stalls for gain during the rush while the son is off.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy time is to stall so as to win an advantage later.

clue.text: Noble player in Varsity match initiated

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsman who has played for Oxford or Cambridge against the other in the Varsity match
to blood a newcomer is to initiate them, so blooded means initiated

explanation.surface: An aristocratic player is given his debut in the Oxford–Cambridge match.
explanation.walkthrough: The Varsity match is the annual Oxford v Cambridge game; those who play win a 'Blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocrats are said to have blue blood, so someone of noble birth is so described.

clue.text: Resilient European to remain in charge

parts.note: to last is to remain or endure

explanation.surface: A tough European manages to stay on as the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material springs back into shape, which is what resilient means.

clue.text: Influenced by articles in Le Monde and Die Welt

parts.note: Le Monde is a French paper; un is the French indefinite article
Die Welt is a German paper; der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: Newspaper articles in France and Germany swayed by somebody's views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' look like newspaper pieces; they are grammatical words, a and the.
explanation.definitionFit: To be under someone's spell is to be swayed or influenced by them.

clue.text: Tried yet failed to acquire by skill

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in, or acquire, the times sign inside them
a failed attempt has gone wrong, so the letters of these two words are muddled

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as by, as in four by two

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to obtain something skilfully and still came up short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' rearranges TRIED YET and 'to acquire' places X within.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexterity is deftness of hand or mind, a skill or adroitness.

clue.text: Ructions as king intercepts saboteur unexpectedly

indicators.note: the king cuts into, or intercepts, the jumbled letters, landing among them
acting unexpectedly, the letters of saboteur come in a surprising new order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Uproar breaks out as a monarch catches a saboteur by surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' muddles SABOTEUR and 'intercepts' slips the K inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ructions are noisy disturbances, and sudden eruptions of violence are their plural kin.

clue.text: Don't hold back with the rent, maybe, sobbing

parts.note: a rent is a rip, a tear, as in a rent in the cloth
not holding back means doing a thing fully, all the way

explanation.surface: A tenant is urged to pay the rent in full, and weeps over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like the payment to a landlord; it is a rip, so not holding back with a rip means ripping fully.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobbing describes crying, in the manner of one weeping with tears.

clue.text: Beefy type turned up in underwear that often snapped

definitions.note: a thing that often snapped: the definition is a descriptive phrase standing for a noun

indicators.note: the beefy type and his arrival sit inside the underwear, wrapped by its letters

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
an ox is a hefty animal raised for beef
to turn up is to come, so turned up is came

explanation.surface: A burly man appears in his underpants and gets photographed a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like a reversal; it simply means arrived. 'snapped' means took photos, not broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple old box-shaped camera took many snapshots; snapping is taking a quick photo.

clue.text: A way into field blocked by black spiky plant

indicators.note: the way into the field is blocked, with the black letter stuck in the middle of it

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for getting over a fence into a field
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A route into a meadow is obstructed by a dark, prickly shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a garden perennial bearing feathery, pointed flower plumes.

clue.text: Peak in Ionian Islands seen from east

indicators.note: in an across clue east is the right-hand end, so reading from the east means right to left
the letters sit inside the words Ionian Islands, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A mountain in the Greek isles viewed from the eastern side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Sinai is the mountain in Egypt where Moses received the commandments.

clue.text: Handle of identical large pot's broken

indicators.note: the word for identical is broken open, with the large pot set inside it

parts.note: identical things are the same
an urn is a large pot or vase

explanation.surface: The handle of a large pot, one of a matching set, has snapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like part of the pot; it is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is informal for a name, and the family name is one such.

clue.text: Dance record by Rolling Stone

indicators.note: rolling stones tumble over, so the letters of stone are turned around into a new order

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A dance track recorded by one of the Rolling Stones.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ballroom dance popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Erected, taken down and mounted

indicators.note: taken downwards, as the entry in this down light is read, it gives the same letters as read upwards

parts.note: to mount an exhibition or a defence is to put one up

explanation.surface: Something put up, then pulled down and set up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken down' looks like the opposite of 'Erected'; it says the phrase for 'mounted' reads the same down as up.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a tent or building is to raise it, a common phrasal verb sense.

clue.text: Log-keeper dismissed, log not started

parts.note: to be fired is to be dismissed from a job

indicators.note: without its start, so the first letter of log is removed

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A ship's log-keeper has been sacked, the log never begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log-keeper' suggests a ship's officer; it holds burning logs.
explanation.definitionFit: An andiron, a metal stand holding logs in a hearth, is also called by this name.

clue.text: Stray dog's lead split

indicators.note: a lead goes in front, so it signals the opening letter of the word dog's

parts.note: a rift is a split or break

explanation.surface: A wandering dog's lead has snapped in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a leash for the stray dog; it gives the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To drift is to wander aimlessly, to stray from a course.

clue.text: Doctor damaging practice

parts.note: ill effects are damaging ones

explanation.surface: A harmful practice in the doctor's surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'practice' looks like a medical practice; it is repeated training.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a repeated exercise, a routine practice.

clue.text: Take vital supply yielding plenty of gas

indicators.note: read as an adverb, supply means in a supple, pliant way, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Take an essential supply of fuel that gives off plenty of gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like provisions; it is 'in a supple way'. 'gas' is idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is slang for chatter, and a chatty person produces plenty of it.

clue.text: Sport losing wife's attention

indicators.note: the word loses the wife's letter, which is dropped from it

parts.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A sports team loses the attention of a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone your ear is to listen with attention.

clue.text: Like deserts, several lacking sun

indicators.note: the word for several lacks the sun, which is removed from its start

parts.note: sundry means various or several
the word sun is the very letters removed

explanation.surface: Deserts compared: several of them have no sun at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts are arid places with little rain, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: Liberal MP enters, yet her children have all gone

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: a parent like her, whose children have left home

indicators.note: a liberal translation is a free one, so the letters are taken freely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician comes into the house, but her children have moved out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party of the MP; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent whose grown-up offspring have left home is so described, like a bird with an empty nest.
